chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn al-Hasayn, from Fadl al-Baqbaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the traveler who stays with some of his family for a day or a night or three days. He said, 'I do not like that he shortens the prayer.'

key_terms.يَوْمًا أَوْ لَيْلَةً أَوْ ثَلَاثًا: A day or a night or three days

ai.seo_question: Should a traveler shorten their prayers if they stay in one place for only a few days?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preference for not shortening prayers (qasr) when a traveler stays with family for up to three days highlights the distinction between the legal permission (ibahah) and the recommended practice (istihbab) in Shia jurisprudence. This view is often cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi to argue that the traveler's status remains that of a traveler regardless of staying with relatives, yet the spiritual benefit of full prayer is preferred. It underscores the principle that while the ruling of qasr applies, the act of performing full prayer (tamam) is more virtuous during short stays.
